description: Baseline cold-cache homepage visual readiness

asi.hypothesis: The baseline will confirm that client-side N+1 user-composition requests and poster transfers dominate visual readiness.
asi.finding: The homepage issued 46 user-composition API requests and transferred 18.2 MB before visual readiness; LCP nearly equals visualReadyMs, while initial HTML and hydration finished under 100 ms.
asi.next_action_hint: Return card-ready metadata in the list response so the homepage does not fetch 45 full Presets individually.

description: Eliminate homepage N+1 full-Preset fetches by returning card metadata in the local list response

asi.hypothesis: Deriving poster key, duration, and surface type while the local server already parses each composition will remove 45 redundant browser requests and reduce client work without caching changing Presets.
asi.finding: User-composition requests fell from 46 to 1 and visual readiness improved by 199 ms (12.9%). The 18.1 MB transfer remains almost entirely poster imagery, and LCP still determines readiness.
asi.user_constraint: Presets are frequently changing local data; hard caching and hardcoded metadata are not acceptable. Continue targeting JavaScript, Svelte rendering, and request scheduling.
asi.next_action_hint: Profile why the browser transfers roughly the entire 15 MB poster corpus on the initial viewport despite lazy loading; fix Svelte/DOM image scheduling rather than caching data.

description: Gate poster image creation with a near-viewport IntersectionObserver attachment

asi.hypothesis: Explicitly mounting only near-viewport images will avoid native lazy-loading's broad preload distance and reduce contention from the dense grid.
asi.finding: LCP improved by 28 ms versus the current best, but overall visual readiness regressed by 43 ms and transfer size barely changed. Chrome still requested nearly the full poster corpus, likely because the first 45-card user section remains within the observer scheduling/layout window or because readiness/network accounting captures subsequent observer intersections.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric worsened by 3.2% versus the current best; added observer complexity did not materially reduce transferred bytes.
asi.next_action_hint: Profile request initiators and poster dimensions/count rather than adding another lazy-load layer. Investigate duplicate full-resolution poster decodes and whether responsive thumbnail generation is the actual bottleneck.

description: Defer poster alpha-crop scans until browser idle so decoded images can paint first

asi.hypothesis: Synchronous per-image alpha scans in load handlers delay Svelte's ready-state paint during a burst of local poster decodes.
asi.finding: The benchmark improved another 70 ms versus the current best and showed only 540 KB of poster data; 18.6 MB total is mostly dev-server script/module overhead. Correctness checks failed without surfaced output because checks.sh suppresses stdout, so the promising change was reverted.
asi.rollback_reason: Required npm check failed; a benchmark improvement cannot be kept with failed checks.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply the idle crop change, run npm check directly to expose and fix the type/compiler error, then rerun. Improve checks.sh so failure output is visible.

description: Move non-critical poster alpha-crop scans out of image load handlers and into browser idle time

asi.hypothesis: Synchronous alpha-crop work in each image load handler blocks Svelte ready-state paints even though the decoded poster is already usable.
asi.finding: Deferring crop refinement improved visual readiness by 48 ms versus the current best and improved LCP by 280 ms. Poster traffic is only 45 requests/540 KB; cold dev-server JavaScript/module traffic is the larger remaining cost.
asi.next_action_hint: Reduce homepage client module graph. The page imports the full preset engine module, eagerly validates 99 JSON files, and pulls editor/runtime dependencies just to render the library.

description: Render the dynamic Preset catalog from server-derived card metadata and lazy-load editor-only modules on user actions

asi.hypothesis: The homepage should not import and validate the full frequently changing Preset corpus or editor/runtime modules merely to render card labels and thumbnails.
asi.finding: Visual readiness improved by 358 ms versus the current best and 605 ms versus baseline. Initial script traffic fell from 6.29 MB to 1.86 MB, preset module traffic fell from 1.12 MB to zero, and total cold dev-server traffic fell by 7.6 MB. Metadata remains derived from live Presets on every server module refresh; nothing is hardcoded or persistently cached.
asi.next_action_hint: Remove the remaining post-mount user-composition list fetch by including server-derived user card metadata in page data, so user cards and poster requests can begin in SSR without a second render.

description: Move user-composition card metadata into homepage SSR through a shared server catalog

asi.hypothesis: Server-rendering user cards will remove the post-mount list request and let visible posters begin sooner.
asi.finding: The API request disappeared, LCP improved 24 ms, and only 26 posters were requested, but sequentially reading, validating, and inspecting 45 user compositions increased TTFB by 38 ms and overall visual readiness regressed 127 ms.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric worsened 13.6% versus the current best. Moving existing sequential work onto the critical server path was counterproductive.
asi.next_action_hint: If revisiting SSR user cards, first make server catalog reads concurrent and provide a card-only lane that does not perform media inspection unused by the homepage. Otherwise keep the client request off the initial critical path.

description: Read and inspect local user-composition metadata concurrently in the collection endpoint

asi.hypothesis: Parallel local file reads and media inspections will shorten the post-mount user-composition request.
asi.finding: The run regressed 129 ms, driven by unrelated-looking initial navigation TTFB growth from 35 ms to 86 ms; API request count and payload were unchanged. Concurrency did not produce a measurable end-to-end win under the primary workload.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric worsened 13.9% versus the current best; do not retain concurrency solely on an unproven micro-optimization.
asi.next_action_hint: Focus on initial render and image priority. Add phase signal for the user-composition response before retrying server endpoint changes.

description: Replace non-reactive poster crop cache SvelteMap with a plain Map

asi.hypothesis: The module cache has no reactive consumers, so a plain Map may avoid unnecessary Svelte invalidation overhead during image-load bursts.
asi.finding: ESLint requires SvelteMap for mutable Maps in components, and the benchmark was substantially worse. The run also had unusually high TTFB/load timing, but there is no evidence this change helps.
asi.rollback_reason: Correctness checks failed on svelte/prefer-svelte-reactivity and primary metric regressed.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep SvelteMap to satisfy project lint. Profile reactive invalidation with tooling before challenging the rule.

description: Add user-composition response timing and confirm the optimized homepage on a repeated cold-browser run

asi.hypothesis: A repeated run with explicit API response timing will separate dev-server variance from user-composition and poster phases.
asi.finding: Unchanged product code measured 810 ms, 123 ms faster than the prior keep, confirming substantial warm dev-server variance. User metadata finished at 379 ms; visible poster/LCP completion followed about 417 ms later. Treat small future differences cautiously and target structural changes larger than this noise.
asi.next_action_hint: Optimize the 379–796 ms image/decode/render phase. Test removing the decorative 300 ms opacity fade, which may delay LCP without helping skeleton readiness.

description: Mount poster images only when their previews intersect the viewport

asi.hypothesis: A zero-margin IntersectionObserver will prevent native lazy loading from prefetching off-screen rows while preserving dynamic poster behavior.
asi.finding: Poster requests fell from 45 to 23, poster bytes fell 43%, and LCP improved 228 ms, but the primary metric was 1.6 ms worse than the current best—well within observed dev-server noise.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric did not improve, and the added attachment should not be kept based only on secondary metrics without confirmation.
asi.next_action_hint: Repeat the exact candidate once as advised for a within-noise result; keep only if primary improvement confirms while request/LCP gains persist.

description: Load dynamic posters only when their card previews actually enter the viewport

asi.hypothesis: Repeating the zero-margin viewport attachment will confirm whether its near-neutral first primary result was noise while preserving large LCP/request reductions.
asi.finding: Confirmed: visual readiness improved 52 ms versus the current best, LCP improved another 296 ms, poster requests fell from 45 to 14, and poster bytes fell 64%. Off-screen dynamic posters still load when scrolled into view; no content or cache is hardcoded.
asi.next_action_hint: The user-composition response now ends around 366 ms and LCP around 500 ms. Investigate whether returning a card-only response can reduce API parse/media inspection without moving work into TTFB.

description: Add a card-only user-composition response that skips media inspection unused by the homepage

asi.hypothesis: The homepage card lane can preserve schema and semantic validation while skipping media filesystem inspection and response fields it never reads.
asi.finding: Visual readiness improved 16.6 ms, API response end improved 16.4 ms, and LCP improved 24 ms. The card response remains derived from each current local Preset and validates it; this is not caching or hardcoding.
asi.next_action_hint: Add focused coverage for the card view contract, then test whether the remaining 300 ms image opacity transition affects perceived readiness or only LCP.

description: Mark observer-confirmed visible posters as high fetch priority

asi.hypothesis: Once IntersectionObserver confirms a poster is visible, high fetch priority may finish its local request and decode sooner.
asi.finding: Primary metric regressed 2.7 ms and LCP regressed 8 ms; the run also requested 23 rather than 14 posters, suggesting priority provided no stable scheduling benefit.
asi.rollback_reason: No primary improvement and no secondary evidence of benefit.
asi.next_action_hint: Leave browser priority automatic. Use the final iteration for focused contract coverage and a confirmation run of the kept state.

description: Decode visible poster images asynchronously

asi.hypothesis: Explicit asynchronous decoding will keep visible poster decodes from blocking the main thread during Svelte's user-card insertion.
asi.finding: Visual readiness improved 18 ms versus the current best and LCP improved 8 ms. User API timing also varied lower, so the gain is modest but the primary metric improved with all checks passing.
asi.next_action_hint: Stop at the user-requested 15-run cap. Add focused card-view contract coverage during normal follow-up rather than another optimization experiment.

description: Preload the dynamic user-composition card response from homepage HTML

asi.hypothesis: Starting the same dynamic card-response fetch from the HTML head will overlap local Preset parsing with hydration and reduce the post-mount wait without caching or hardcoding data.
asi.finding: The card response ended only 9 ms earlier, while DOMContentLoaded regressed by about 390 ms and visual readiness regressed by 899 ms. Preloading the CPU-heavy local endpoint competed with critical dev-server module transformation and hydration rather than creating useful overlap.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric more than doubled; eager preload moved non-critical local parsing onto the critical path.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep user-composition loading after mount. Future work should reduce endpoint CPU cost or use true server streaming, not raise its network priority.

description: Read and validate local user compositions concurrently for the card endpoint

asi.hypothesis: Parallel filesystem reads will reduce the card endpoint's response time while retaining full schema and semantic validation of frequently changing local Presets.
asi.finding: The user-composition response ended 9 ms later than the current best, LCP regressed 40 ms, and visual readiness regressed 23 ms. Concurrent reads did not help because validation and hashing remain CPU-bound on the single JavaScript thread, while extra promise scheduling added overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric worsened 3.2% and the endpoint-specific timing also regressed.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep sequential reads. A meaningful endpoint improvement requires reducing repeated CPU validation/hashing work through an invalidation-safe design, not parallelizing local I/O.

description: Load Graffiti only on the workspace route instead of the homepage layout

asi.hypothesis: The homepage fully restyles its controls and should not load the workspace-oriented Graffiti package globally; route-scoping it may shrink cold dev-server work without changing workspace behavior.
asi.finding: Total response traffic fell by about 361 KB, confirming Graffiti contributed avoidable homepage bytes, but visual readiness regressed 40 ms, LCP regressed 40 ms, and the user API completed 59 ms later. The byte reduction did not translate into the primary metric under this workload.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric worsened 5.6%; do not retain a dependency-boundary refactor based only on transferred bytes.
asi.next_action_hint: Profile the client main-thread timeline or endpoint CPU directly before another structural change. Remaining differences are now close to dev-server variance.

description: Remove redundant native lazy loading after the viewport observer mounts a poster

asi.hypothesis: The zero-margin IntersectionObserver already prevents off-screen image creation, so native loading="lazy" adds a second scheduler delay to images known to be visible.
asi.finding: Visual readiness improved 10 ms versus the current best with unchanged API and transfer characteristics. LCP varied 28 ms worse, so the gain is modest, but the primary metric improved and the code is simpler: the observer now solely owns deferred loading.
asi.next_action_hint: Confirm the small gain on a repeat before building further on it; observed dev-server noise is of similar magnitude.

description: Repeat the observer-only poster loading result to measure its stability

asi.hypothesis: A repeat of the unchanged observer-only image-loading path will show whether iteration 19's 10 ms primary improvement exceeds dev-server noise.
asi.finding: The unchanged code measured 719 ms, 5.7 ms slower than iteration 19 but still 4.4 ms faster than the prior 723 ms best. LCP improved from 496 ms to 472 ms. This confirms the change is at least neutral-to-positive, while the exact 10 ms gain is within run noise.
asi.rollback_reason: No new product change was under test and the repeated primary value did not beat the current recorded best.
asi.next_action_hint: Retain iteration 19 because it simplifies scheduling and remains slightly ahead of the previous implementation across the repeat; require larger structural gains for future keeps.

description: Split homepage card metadata into a dedicated lightweight API route

asi.hypothesis: A dedicated card endpoint will avoid loading the full collection route's media-inspection and write dependencies during the homepage request while preserving live schema and semantic validation.
asi.finding: Visual readiness regressed 14 ms and initial script/response traffic was unchanged, showing that the shared Preset schema and semantic-validation graph—not the omitted route dependencies—dominates this dev-server request. The API-specific probe matched only the old URL, so its zero values are instrumentation gaps; the primary network-idle metric still covered the new request.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric worsened 1.9% and no transfer reduction supported the added route/module complexity.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the existing card query lane. Further endpoint splitting is unlikely to help unless Preset validation itself is moved off the request path with safe invalidation.

description: Memoize validated card metadata with filesystem-signature invalidation

asi.hypothesis: A process-local card metadata cache keyed by inode, size, mtime, and ctime can skip repeated schema validation and hashing while immediately invalidating whenever frequently edited local Presets change.
asi.finding: The API response ended 7.7 ms earlier, but per-file stat checks and overall timing produced a 13 ms visual-readiness regression. The small endpoint gain did not justify cache state or its invalidation complexity, especially given the user's preference against caching as the solution.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric worsened 1.8%; discard the cache despite its safe invalidation and modest API improvement.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not pursue metadata caching. Remaining work should target first-request CPU cost directly or stop when gains are below noise.

description: Skip off-screen homepage section rendering with CSS content visibility

asi.hypothesis: Applying content-visibility:auto to library sections will let the browser skip style, paint, and rendering work for off-screen composition groups without removing content or changing dynamic loading.
asi.finding: LCP improved 36 ms and the user API ended 8.6 ms earlier, but visual readiness was 3.1 ms slower than the current best. The primary difference is within noise, and transferred resources were unchanged.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric did not improve; avoid retaining intrinsic-size/layout behavior solely for secondary gains without a confirmed end-to-end benefit.
asi.next_action_hint: If off-screen rendering remains interesting, repeat with profiling rather than relying on a sub-5 ms primary difference. Current best likely represents the practical floor of this dev workload.

description: Store user-composition API results in shallow Svelte state

asi.hypothesis: User-composition card metadata is only replaced as a whole, so $state.raw should avoid unnecessary deep proxy creation for the 45-object API response while preserving reactive assignments and deletion.
asi.finding: Visual readiness was 2.4 ms slower than the current best and the API response itself arrived 16 ms later; any proxy savings were below dev-server noise. Functionality and checks remained correct.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric did not improve, so the state-style cleanup was reverted under the experiment rules.
asi.next_action_hint: Proxy creation is not a meaningful bottleneck at this data size. Avoid micro-optimizing Svelte state without direct profile evidence.

description: Cancel unfinished poster requests when layout shifts cards off-screen

asi.hypothesis: Keeping the viewport observer active until image load will unmount and cancel template poster requests that become off-screen when user cards insert above them, eliminating wasted dynamic-layout traffic.
asi.finding: Poster request count and bytes were unchanged, showing those requests complete before the layout shift or are retained by Chrome despite image unmounting. Extra observer lifecycle work regressed visual readiness by 18 ms.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric worsened 2.6%, with no reduction in the targeted request or byte metrics.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not add cancellation state to PosterCard. Initial template requests are not the remaining bottleneck under local network conditions.

description: Validate user card metadata with a type guard without cloning every entry

asi.hypothesis: Replacing flatMap plus per-entry array/object allocations with a type-guard filter will reduce client work when the card response is inserted into Svelte state while preserving trust-boundary validation.
asi.finding: Visual readiness regressed 38 ms and LCP regressed 20 ms. The user API also arrived 30 ms later, dominating the result; any client allocation reduction was not measurable end to end.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric worsened 5.3%, so the parser refactor was reverted despite being allocation-light.
asi.next_action_hint: Client parsing of 45 metadata objects is not worth further micro-optimization. Remaining variance is dominated by server/API timing.

description: Start the user-card request during component initialization before grid hydration

asi.hypothesis: Starting a fresh per-instance card request when the client component initializes—after its module loads but before the large grid hydrates—will avoid onMount scheduling delay without the critical-path competition caused by HTML preload.
asi.finding: The API response did not arrive earlier and visual readiness regressed 44 ms. Component initialization and onMount are already close enough that the earlier fetch only competed with hydration and poster scheduling.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric worsened 6.2%, with no improvement in the targeted API response end.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the post-mount request. Request start scheduling is not the remaining bottleneck; direct tracing is required before changing it again.

description: Replace repainting skeleton shimmers with a static placeholder

asi.hypothesis: Animating background-position across every unresolved card repaints many skeleton surfaces during hydration and image decode; a static visible placeholder should remove that paint pressure without hiding readiness.
asi.finding: LCP improved 60 ms to the best observed 436 ms, but visual readiness regressed 40 ms because navigation and API timing were slower. The primary result did not confirm an end-to-end gain despite the promising paint-side signal.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric worsened 5.6%; under the experiment rules the static-placeholder change cannot be retained on LCP alone.
asi.next_action_hint: A controlled repeat could determine whether the LCP gain is real, but primary readiness is now dominated by timing variance outside skeleton paint.

description: Repeat the static skeleton placeholder experiment

asi.hypothesis: Repeating the static skeleton candidate will determine whether iteration 28's 60 ms LCP gain reflects reduced repaint pressure or ordinary dev-server variance.
asi.finding: LCP was only 12 ms better than the current kept state rather than the prior 60 ms signal, and visual readiness remained 1.9 ms slower than the best. The large iteration 28 LCP improvement did not reproduce.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric again failed to improve, and the secondary gain was not stable enough to justify changing the loading treatment.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the existing shimmer. Skeleton animation is not a confirmed bottleneck; avoid further repeats without a paint trace.

description: Show decoded posters immediately instead of fading them in over 300 ms

asi.hypothesis: Once a poster's load event removes its skeleton, a 300 ms opacity transition delays useful pixels and LCP without conveying meaningful state; immediate display should improve perceived readiness and reduce compositing work.
asi.finding: LCP improved 72 ms to the best observed 424 ms and the API timing matched the current best, but the primary network-idle readiness metric was 10 ms slower. The visual improvement is real, but it did not satisfy the session's primary keep criterion.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric worsened 1.4%; under the configured rules the fade removal was reverted despite the strong LCP gain.
asi.next_action_hint: The primary metric's 300 ms network-idle tail now diverges from perceived readiness. Do not change the metric mid-session, but consider a future separate LCP-focused session if immediate poster display is the product priority.

description: Start visible poster requests from a post-DOM microtask instead of waiting for observer delivery

asi.hypothesis: A batched post-DOM geometry check can identify actually visible cards before IntersectionObserver's asynchronous callback, starting their poster requests roughly one frame earlier without hardcoded card counts or viewport assumptions.
asi.finding: Visual readiness was 1.3 ms slower than the current best, LCP was unchanged, and poster request counts/bytes were unchanged. Any observer delivery delay is below the workload's timing noise; geometry checks only added code and bytes.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric did not improve and no targeted secondary signal changed.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep IntersectionObserver as the sole visibility mechanism. Poster request dispatch is not measurably late.

description: Repeat immediate poster display without the opacity fade

asi.hypothesis: Repeating fade removal will confirm whether its large LCP improvement can coexist with a primary readiness win once API timing variance settles.
asi.finding: LCP again improved, this time by 36 ms, but visual readiness again regressed by about 10 ms. Two runs now show the same trade-off: immediate display improves perceived paint timing but not the session's network-idle primary metric.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric failed to improve on the confirmation run, so fade removal was reverted again.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not repeat fade removal in this session. Its value belongs in a separately configured LCP/perceived-readiness experiment.

description: Instrument composition versus surface poster traffic on the kept homepage

asi.hypothesis: Separating surface fallback traffic from composition poster traffic will identify whether duplicate fallback images or real visible previews determine the network-idle tail.
asi.finding: Of 23 poster requests, only 2 requests/5.4 KB were surface fallbacks; 21 requests/302.7 KB were actual composition previews. The remaining poster traffic is useful visible content, not duplicate fallback waste. Unchanged product code measured 728 ms, within established dev-server variance but above the current best.
asi.rollback_reason: No product change was tested and the repeated primary value did not beat the current best.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not optimize surface fallbacks. Any further network-tail reduction must make the 21 real composition thumbnails smaller/faster without lowering visual quality, or use a different primary metric.

description: Send per-card poster availability instead of the full poster-key corpus

asi.hypothesis: Replacing the serialized set of roughly 1,146 poster keys with per-card availability booleans will reduce homepage payload and client Set construction while still deriving every value from the live local poster store.
asi.finding: Total response traffic fell by about 19 KB, but the card API ended 28 ms later because it had to read the poster directory again after mount. Visual readiness regressed 19 ms; the duplicated filesystem lookup outweighed serialization savings.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric worsened 2.6%, and API timing confirmed the architectural trade-off was negative.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the single server-loaded poster-key set. Its small payload is cheaper than repeating poster-store discovery in the card endpoint.

description: Stream user-composition cards from server load instead of fetching after mount

asi.hypothesis: Starting the internal card endpoint during server load and streaming its promise will overlap filesystem validation with SSR, eliminate the browser API request, and avoid blocking initial page fields behind an await.
asi.finding: The browser API request disappeared, composition poster requests fell from 21 to 12, poster bytes fell 37%, and LCP improved 28 ms. However the streamed document kept DOMContentLoaded about 38 ms later, leaving primary visual readiness 4.9 ms slower than the current best.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric did not improve; the streaming trade-off shifted work into document completion despite strong request and LCP reductions.
asi.next_action_hint: Streaming is promising for perceived paint but incompatible with the current readyState/network-idle primary. Do not retry without a separate metric or a rendering design that does not hold document completion.

description: Add explicit content lengths to poster image responses

asi.hypothesis: Explicit Content-Length headers on 21 local poster responses will avoid chunked-transfer completion overhead and let Chrome recognize image completion sooner without changing bytes, quality, or caching.
asi.finding: Visual readiness regressed 25 ms; request count was unchanged and encoded poster bytes changed only by header accounting. Explicit lengths did not improve local image completion.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric worsened 3.6%, so the header change was reverted.
asi.next_action_hint: Poster HTTP framing is not the bottleneck. Avoid further micro-optimizations without request-level timing traces.

description: Instrument poster completion timing on the kept homepage

asi.hypothesis: Request-level poster timing will show whether one unusually slow image or the aggregate request wave determines the 300 ms network-idle tail.
asi.finding: The final poster completed at 428 ms, while the slowest individual poster took only 36.7 ms. The card API ended at 351 ms, leaving a 77 ms post-API poster wave before the fixed 300 ms idle window. No single large/slow poster dominates; scheduling roughly 20 useful composition requests after layout insertion determines the tail.
asi.rollback_reason: No product change was tested and the unchanged primary value did not beat the current best.
asi.next_action_hint: Target layout-stabilization waste: avoid starting built-in template posters that are immediately pushed off-screen when user cards arrive, without reducing visible final previews.
